items.text: Fixed in the tab options, each seen in a local build: the "Close other tabs" preview lists every tab that stays open, with the reason; the group picker opened from "Search all tabs" no longer closes that search; "Move to start" and "Move to end" for a grouped tab stay inside its group and say so; the menu key and Shift+F10 open one menu, not two, and Escape gives focus back; search and name fields in the tab panels take focus when they open; the selected tab scrolls fully into view; the automation editor's save bar sits at the page bottom with a bottom strip.
New: "Tab strip position" in Profile chooses the edge the tab strip docks to.

New: a settings page or a tool chosen in the New tab catalog opens as a tab of its own, on the wide strip and in the phone Pages sheet. Choosing it again goes to the tab it already has. Closing the tab in use goes to the neighbouring tab.

New: the tabs of a settings section have their own right-click menu (also the menu key and a long press), groups, their own look, locks, hide by text with a preview and undo, and a search in the More list; they are listed in "Search all tabs". The phone Pages sheet has groups as foldable sections, per-page looks and locks. All seen in a local build at 1440, 1000, 390 and 320 px, in the dark theme, right to left, Cantonese and both languages.

Known small points: "Search all tabs" names a section by its address, not its page name; in both-languages mode one placeholder in the hide dialog is cut; the phone sheet lists groups before loose pages while the wide strip keeps a group at its place in the order.

New: tab options. The tab strip can be docked to the left, right, top or bottom (a new installation starts on the left; an existing one stays at the top until changed). Tabs can be pinned, grouped (name, colour, look, collapse, lock), given their own look, locked, moved and closed in bulk with a preview of what closes and what is protected. An overflow button lists tabs that do not fit. There are four separate searches, each with the pattern builder: this strip, inside a group, group names, and every open tab (Alt+Shift+F). A tab has its own right-click menu, also on the menu key and on a long press.

New: the tabs of a settings section are real tabs with arrow-key movement, a "More tabs" list when they do not fit, pin, hide, reorder and "Open every tab", saved per section. On a phone, the Pages sheet has per-page actions, a pinned group, drag reordering and bulk close with a preview.

New: installing an app from the app store shows a progress bar with its steps and a log terminal (follow, pause, search with the pattern builder, level filter, copy, export). The store card and the activity tray show the same progress, and it is still there after leaving the page. Seen in a running full-mode instance at phone and desktop width. The Supervisor reports a percentage only, so no layer list is shown.

New: a picture, video or audio file can be dropped on any page. An overlay offers Media or Images, the upload shows in the activity tray, and a message offers to open where the files went. Pages with their own drop area keep it; same-name files are skipped, never replaced; only an administrator can add media. Seen in a local build with simulated drags.

Changed: uploads can be larger: 2 GB for the media library (was 20 MB) and 50 MB for the image store (was 10 MB), with a percentage while a file uploads. A reverse proxy in front of the instance may have its own limit. A dropped picture the image store cannot take as it is (WebP, BMP, AVIF) is converted to PNG, and a picture over the limit is re-encoded or resized to fit; the result says what was converted and what was lost. Animated GIFs are never flattened, and large audio or video is not converted. Seen in a local build.

New: "Add media" for phones and keyboards, since a phone cannot drag: in the Pages sheet menu on a phone, the Media page toolbar, the activity tray and the quick bar. It opens the system picker and follows the same path as a drop. Pasting a picture, video or audio file on a page does the same, except inside text fields and editors. The toolbar entry and paste were seen at phone width in a local build; the Pages sheet entry was not.

New: the image store has folders. From Manage in the Media page: New folder, open with a breadcrumb, rename, move images, remove a folder (its images move up, none is deleted). Image addresses do not change, so pictures used by people, areas and dashboards keep working. Uploads go into the folder being looked at.

New: in Manage, for media and images: download an item, download a selection as one zip (up to 200 MB), edit a name (a taken name is refused), and convert an item with the built-in converter into a new item beside the original. The image store keeps PNG and JPEG results only.

New: the dim sum surprise. One launch in ten shows a small card with one dish, its picture and its name in English and Cantonese; it never takes focus and closes by itself. Personal settings has its switch, which cannot be turned off. School mode hides all of it. One download in ten of a single item arrives as a zip holding the file unchanged plus one dish picture, and says so. Pictures come only from the public dim sum catalogue: the server fetches them with a plain request that carries nothing about the instance and keeps them in its own storage. This is the one feature that contacts an outside address.
New: when a repair fails, the repair dialog says so, and says separately when the failed repair left new issues behind.

Changed: in "full" hosting mode the checks that can never pass inside a container (no operating system, no systemd, no NetworkManager, no AppArmor and so on) are no longer reported as "Unsupported system" repairs; every other check still runs. Seen on a throwaway instance: nine reasons before, none after. An existing instance needs the new outer image and Supervisor. The unsupported-installation dialog explains each reason in one sentence and has no outside links.
Deploy Assistant: with a wording file in use, a new deployment's container and Compose project are named with the file's word for that kind of deployment.

Fixed: in build 122 every toast message was pushed sideways and upward, so its buttons were off the screen on a phone. Build 122 should be skipped. Seen fixed in a local build: one toast and a stack of three sit centred above the bottom bar at 390, 320 and 1440 px.

Fixed: an operating system update was called finished about 40 seconds after it started, before any restart (seen on a real update from 18.5.109 to 18.5.121 in a virtual machine, which otherwise worked: the update was verified with this project's certificate, the machine came back in two minutes on the second boot slot, and the core update showed a real percentage). It now ends with "Installed. Restart to finish", a Restart now button and a Later choice, and says "is now on version" only when that version is running. Not yet seen in a running build.
Changed: "Reboot system", "Shut down system" and "Move data disk" show only where the Supervisor says it can do them; the app store's Repositories page lists the built-in repositories.

Fixed, from the browser pass on build 122 (39 of 47 earlier defects were already seen fixed there): toolbar chips are no longer cut; a row's checkbox can be tapped 44 px high; the statistics strip's "Shown" follows the typed search; sub-tab labels never break inside a word; the page catalog has its titles when opened from any page; the automation editor's bottom bar is 113 px on a phone, down from 177; the Blueprints note holds its link; Delete and the menu buttons on the dark selection bar are readable; dialog buttons and "Done" are 44 px on touch; a blueprint that cannot be fetched again says why. All but the last were measured in a local build.

"Full" hosting mode was run end to end with the published images of release 122 (`host.bat --full`), and rehearsed with a copy of a real instance's settings; the copy needs the core's port changed to 80, which the documented command now does.

New: a second way to host the product, "full" mode (`host.bat --full`). One outer container runs its own small Docker engine; inside it the Supervisor, the core and every app run as containers of their own, so the app store, apps opening inside the interface, full backups that include apps and real updates work, while the computer sees one container. Run for real on a throwaway copy: 96 apps listed from 5 repositories; File editor, Mosquitto, Terminal and SSH and a community app installed, started and opened at 390 and 1440 px; a third-party repository added; a full backup with apps restored; the core updated from 2026.11.1.53 to 2026.11.1.118 through the interface; stop and start brought everything back; the host restart and shutdown controls only return an error and the computer is untouched. It needs a privileged container, about 745 MB of memory idle and 7 to 8.4 GB of disk. It needs the Supervisor image of THIS release or later (the published 2026.11.0.118 reports itself unhealthy in this mode); the job that publishes the outer image has not run yet. See `docs/features/hosting/full-mode.md`.

Release 2026.11.1.121 was the first published under the rule that nothing is published until every build job of the run has succeeded: 25 files in one step, and the update feed moved with it (operating system 18.5.121 for all four boards).

Fixed: a dashboard page that holds a single card (each room page of an Overview that was made editable) had nothing to add content with. In edit mode it now says so at the top and offers "Use sections layout", which turns it into a sections page; a page that is still generated offers "Make editable copy". The page uses the visible screen height, so its edit bar no longer slides under the phone's bottom bar. Seen in a local build at 390, 320 and 1440 px.

Fixed, found by looking at build 121 in a browser: the statistics strip was built but no page used it (it is on Devices, Entities, Automations, Scripts, Helpers and Tags now); selection bar buttons and row checkboxes were under 44 px on a touch screen; the bar covered the row of sub-tabs on a phone; a long press on a dashboard tile opened nothing (a hold action a person set is never taken over); "Select all", "Invert" and a toast's action were hard to read on the dark bar; the stack of toasts covered the bottom bar; the type scale was lost on reload and made headings smaller when switched on; support ticket notes did not follow the account; the phone's page catalog had no groups; the worked example and practise control were used by no page (they are on the General page and in guided setup now); dashboard edit mode on a phone listed tools that do not belong there; the script editor always showed its save bar. Not yet seen in a running build.

Fixed, from the polish list seen in build 121: no empty box at the end of a Users row on a phone; the Blueprints note has room; Personal settings marks its first section before any scroll. Not yet seen in a running build.

Fixed: backups made by official Home Assistant releases. Backups from 2026.11.1, 2025.1.4 and 2024.6.4 were restored through the interface, at first-run setup and from the Backups page, with users, helpers, an automation, a script, a scene, a dashboard, an area and history all kept. Five gaps found there are fixed: an older archive whose inner file name starts with "./" was refused as a wrong password; a backup from a newer release was refused only after the core had stopped (it is refused before anything stops now); a later patch release of the same month is accepted and a backup made here carries the three-part core version, so official builds accept it; a name with a slash is tidied instead of refused; the first-run restore page no longer lists two lines twice. The fixes are covered by server tests and were checked against ten real backup files; they are not yet seen through the interface. Not exercised: a real Home Assistant OS backup with apps, cloud backups and databases older than 2024.6.

Fixed, from the design lane's boards of the running interface: bottom bar labels are no longer cut on a phone; a narrow table row shows two lines of secondary text; Settings tile descriptions get two lines; the Users page on a phone keeps the avatar beside the name, its footnote wraps and its "Active" header has room; the Updates row without an Update button lines up with the others; Personal settings marks the section in view; the "Learn more" pill on the Home banner is readable in the dark scheme; the selected page tab is never under the edge fade; Select is clear of the Add device button; Blueprints descriptions wrap on a phone; the automation history table head stays on one line; the Overview no longer has an empty cell where a home has no power sensor. Not yet seen in a running build.

Fixed in the Deploy Assistant: Instances, Downloads and Extensions have a one-line description; instance card lines wrap and paths break only at separators; the chart's waiting label is clear of the gridline; the tab strip fades where it is cut; model row buttons line up; the Deploy header wraps evenly. Seen in the app's browser demo at 1280 and 400 px, not in the packaged app.

New: the dashboard header carries the page tools cluster. View mode uses the shared cluster (one overflow button on a phone). Edit mode shows appearance, history, export and help, locked mode shows only Unlock, and embedded dashboards show no cluster. Search this page is not shown in edit mode, and on a phone in edit mode the shared overflow panel may still list lock and read aloud. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: the first-run integrations step has a failure-safe state machine and shows discovered integrations as cards, each with a switch, a Set up button, a status chip and a result line. A flow that fails, is cancelled or never answers (15 minute limit) ends in a normal state, and Skip and Finish are never disabled. Cantonese strings added. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: guided setup keeps a draft for 14 days, refuses a jump past invalid options, has a Save and close button, and shows the step list as a column beside the content on a wide screen. The leave text no longer claims drafts follow the account. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: Nest registration guidance in Google setup, a six-step checklist with copyable outside addresses shown as plain text, a live project ID check, a redirect address, and a pasted client file checked and held in memory only. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: a Tickets section on the Support page with create, list, status filter, search, read, notes and close or reopen. Tickets and notes stay on this instance or in this browser. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: command search keyboard operation. Up and Down wrap, Space toggles the live switch on the active row, Escape closes on an empty query, the active row has a visible ring and a polite status line, and three entries were added (personal wording file, accessibility tools, language mode). Not yet seen in a running build.
Fix: the Cantonese source now covers the new onboarding, Google setup and guided setup keys. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: a type scale in the fonts dialog. A switch turns it on, a ratio (1.125, 1.2, 1.25, 1.333 or custom) and a base size set five steps (caption, body, title, headline, display) with an optional size for each step, a live preview and a note that it multiplies with Text size. It is off by default and writes nothing then; reset fonts also resets it. It is applied at startup. Sync through the appearance settings and Cantonese strings for the scale are not done. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: type fields in the appearance editor. Typeface, weight, italic, line height, letter spacing, capitals, alignment and maximum lines each have a reset button and apply live to the picked element, and a warning shows when the resulting text is under 12 px. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: a named palette in both colour tools. 48 named colours, a nearest-name line, sRGB, Display P3 and outside chips (Display P3 is an estimate) and a rainbow hue strip with keyboard control, in the Colour tool and the editor picker. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: a worked example and a practise control in the setting information panel. The practise control (switch, number or text) validates live and states that nothing is saved or sent; the panel keeps focus inside while open. No page supplies an example yet. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: a separate search for each group of the New tab catalog (Pinned, Pages, Settings and Tools), each with a count and its own pattern workbench. Pinned and Pages have a Close matching button that acts only on that group, with Undo. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: the General settings page explains itself. Each of its eight settings has an information button, and the seven that have a default show a Reset, after a confirmation, when they differ from it. Reset only changes the unsaved draft. Not yet seen in a running build.
Fix: the Cantonese source now covers the colour palette and General page help blocks.

New: named test cases and a simulated run in the history manager. A Test cases card keeps named cases for one automation in this browser (fake states, variables and an expected outcome), with rename, duplicate and delete. A simulated run decides state, numeric state, trigger, and, or and not conditions against the fake states only, reports unknown with a reason where it cannot decide, lists the actions that would run and calls no service. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: a dry run of a whole automation and a bottom bar with Run now, Check, Dry run and Save in the automation editor. Each step is listed as would run, would skip or cannot tell, and no service is called. The visual and blueprint editors still draw their own save bar, so two bars show there. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: a repository strip in the automation editor shows the short commit id and time, whether the saved copy matches the live configuration, the number of versions and the remote host only. The repository page has a Push action that asks first and shows the server reply. Pull and an unpushed count are not available because the server has no such data. Not yet seen in a running build.

Changed: the save bar in the script and scene editors hides when nothing changed, has a Discard changes button that uses the existing unsaved-changes question, and announces Saved or the failure message. Try it in the scene editor has its own row. Not yet seen in a running build.
New: tests that check a backup carries every automation repository with its history. They are written and have not been run, because this machine has no securetar. Not yet seen in a running build.
New: starting points for an empty automation and an empty script, six each, shown only while the editor is empty. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: toasts stack. Up to three show at once with the newest nearest the bottom edge and older ones scaled down; the rest wait in a queue behind an "N more waiting" chip. Each toast has its own timer that pauses on hover or focus, an identical anonymous message within two seconds is dropped, errors, warnings and progress stay until dismissed, and one polite live region reads only the newest. Under reduced motion toasts fade only. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: notifications are coloured by severity. The level comes only from an explicit marker at the start of the notification id (error, warning or info), or from the known prefixes update_fail, repair_ and system_; words in the title or message are never read. Rows show an edge, an icon and the severity word, a chip group filters by severity and the list sorts by severity, then newest first. Not yet seen in a running build.
New: a collapsible statistics strip is available on list layouts through an optional statistics property. The folded or open choice is kept per page. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: draft recovery for the template editor. A draft is saved shortly after typing stops and a banner offers Restore, Compare and Discard. Text that looks like a secret, empty text and text over 200 KB are never stored. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: update installs appear as rows in the activity tray with the stage, a progress bar when a percentage is reported, a recovery card with Try again after a failure, and Show update to reopen the update dialog. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: the menu on an element gains entries for what was clicked: Open details, Turn on or Turn off, Copy entity ID, Rename and Hide for entities, and Open the page and Copy ID for devices and areas. Not yet seen in a running build.

New: the shared selection bar is on six more tables. Tags (delete, with a warning for tags an automation tag trigger still uses), Dashboards (show in the sidebar, hide from it, delete), Resources (delete, with the address or outside host of each), Scenes (move to a category, add or remove a label, move to an area, apply, delete), Blueprints (re-import from the saved address, delete, skipping blueprints still in use) and Backups (delete, with a line for the newest backup and one for backups held in a single location). Every destructive action shows a preview of names first, asks twice, runs each item separately and names any that failed, which stay selected. Not yet seen in a running build.

Fixed: on a touch screen a slider reacted only in its middle 32 px, a compact text field was 32 px high and the filter chips beside a table's search field were 32 px high; all are 44 px for a finger now. The colour field's marker no longer covers the Hue label when the colour is black. Not yet seen in a running build.

Seen in build 119: the messages that showed a translation error are fixed (no formatting errors in the log, against 7,764 before), information buttons have proper names, one tap selects a notification and Shift selects a range, the cover of a lock that is locked on start appeared in ten fresh browsers out of ten, and two tabs or two accounts no longer upload each other's settings.

Changed: every personal setting is now saved on this instance for your account and follows you to every device: preferences, schedules, locks, table layouts, saved patterns, change history, the app name and logo and tool drafts. Sign-in tokens, caches and a few per-device switches stay in the browser. Because locks follow the account, clearing browser data no longer removes a forgotten lock; the documentation gives the way back. Seen in a local build, not yet in a published one.
Fixed: a lock could not be created when the instance is opened over plain http on the home network ("The lock could not be created"). Seen working in a local build.
Changed: a lock is named by its card's label or heading, not by all the text on it.
New: a schedule rule can depend on an entity: is, is not, above or below a value, alone or together with a time window.
Changed: dropdowns, sliders, checkboxes, radio buttons and colour choices that were plain browser controls now use the product's own controls, starting with Defaults for everyone.

Fixed: seven messages showed "Translation error"; ticking a notification did not select it; the cover of a lock that is locked on start did not always appear on a fresh browser; the title on the YAML tools page was cut short. Not yet seen in a running build.
Changed: a release is published only after every build job of its run has succeeded. A run that fails or is cancelled publishes nothing. Not yet run.

Fixed: Personal settings on a phone could be dragged sideways until the settings left the screen. The row of group chips was as wide as all its chips (666 px in a 358 px page) and made the page wider than the screen; it now keeps to the page and scrolls inside itself. Seen in a local build.
Changed: on a phone the slim bar at the top that named the current page is gone; the Pages button in the bottom bar switches pages and every page has its own header. Seen in build 115.
Changed: the menu on a phone has less empty space above its title, around the Assist button and between its groups. Seen in build 115.
Fixed: the YAML tools page showed two cramped columns on a phone, with names broken inside words. It is one column until two columns of a comfortable width fit. Seen in build 115.

Fixed: a Minecraft server of version 26.1 or newer could not start, because every server used an image with Java 21 and those versions need Java 25 (found by starting 26.3 for real). The image now follows the game version: Java 25 for 26.1 and newer, 21 for 1.20.5 to 1.21.x, 17 for 1.17 to 1.20.4 and 8 for older versions. The Java 25 image was run by hand and started vanilla 26.3 and Paper 26.3, and in build 111 26.3, 1.21.8, 1.20.1 and 1.16.5 all started through the manager on their own Java.

New: the embedded page panel has a "Page not showing?" button. A page that refuses to be shown inside another page looks loaded to the browser, so no notice appeared by itself; the button explains it. Seen in build 111.
Fixed: when no Ollama server answers, the Models section says so. It used to say the server had no models. Seen in build 111.

Changed: the passkey documentation and message now say that a fresh sign-in, with the password or with a passkey, is what allows adding a passkey; that is how it has always behaved. Passkeys were run end to end in build 109 with a browser virtual authenticator.

Fixed: refreshing the Minecraft version list always failed for Paper, because the service retired the address the list came from. It now uses the service's current address. Found by running the manager against a real SSH and Docker host (a throwaway container), where host trust, a real start, logs, stop, restart and every refusal worked.
Fixed: Enter in a one-line name prompt (for example New folder) now confirms it, except in a prompt that deletes something. Seen in build 109.

Fixed: cells in the Ollama models table no longer break inside words on a narrow screen; the table scrolls sideways instead. Found by running the pages against a real Ollama server, where listing, pull, cancel, delete, unload and the test chat worked. Seen in build 109.

New: Activity has a permanent record. Everything the Activity page shows is also written to a Git repository in the configuration folder, one folder of chunk files for each day, committed in batches (every ten minutes and at shutdown) and never purged, rewritten or squashed. A Permanent record page lists the days, shows a day, searches one day or all days and holds the Git remote settings; nothing leaves the instance unless an administrator sets a remote and pushes. It grows for ever by design, and the folder is included in backups. It can still lose entries in the ways its documentation lists (a power cut in the seconds before a flush, a real queue overflow, shutdown while the disk is failing) and it does not import entries from before it started. Run for real on a throwaway copy across two restarts, and on the hosted instance (build 106) where it created its repository and first day file. The page was seen in build 106 at 390 px wide, showing status Recording, counts and one day.

Fixed: a failed write no longer discards entries from the permanent record (they return to the front of the queue and are retried), a bad entry no longer takes its whole batch with it, a drop is counted only on a real overflow and kept on disk, and a deleted or edited day file is restored from the last commit with a copy of the edited file kept beside it.
Changed: rows in the expanded menu are 48 px high so the whole menu fits a phone screen; the collapsed rail keeps 56 px. Seen in build 106 at 390 px wide.

Fixed: a request naming "." as a media folder could resolve to the media directory itself, so a recursive delete could remove it. Any "." component and the source root are now refused; the counts a person confirmed are enforced, uploads and deletes no longer follow a linked directory out of the media folder, and errors no longer send a server path. The Manage dialog is for administrators only. Server tests: 141 pass.

Fixed: the paid cloud service is hidden in the interface without changing anyone's configuration. A voice pipeline already set to a cloud engine keeps showing it, a configured cloud backup location is hidden but never offered for deletion and is kept when settings are saved, and the network form no longer saves a cloud address as a custom external URL. It remains visible in a few places for someone who has it configured (an existing backup's location name, one entity filter). Eight file fields use a visually hidden field that phones open reliably.

Fixed: a hostile TAR file with a negative size no longer makes the file converter loop for ever, a photo's rotation is read only from its Exif block, pictures going into a PDF stay compressed and are capped, audio conversion can be cancelled and every wait has a time limit, long odd text no longer freezes the page, and names with direction overrides or control characters are refused or cleaned.

Fixed: Enter on the buttons inside the version picker's search field no longer picks a version, the picker no longer raises the keyboard by itself on a touch screen, and a slow compare answer can no longer replace a newer one. The bottom navigation bar publishes its visible height so the editor save bar, the accessibility panel and the picker stop reserving room for it while it is hidden. A group chip on the personal settings page no longer scrolls its title under the pinned chips, and accessibility panel buttons are at least 44 px. Not yet seen in a running build.

Seen in a running build (build 103, 390 px wide, signed in with a generated test account on a throwaway copy): the file converter (categories show Ready), the support page, the Minecraft servers empty state, the profile security page with the authenticator card, the Ollama empty state, the updates page, media sources, the dashboard history overview with its search field and correct plural forms, and the voice assistants page with no cloud promotion. Fixed after: a tab's version count wrapped onto two lines.

Fixed: "Add media" did nothing on a phone because the file field sat outside the open dialog; it now lives inside the button, uploads to the image upload folder, and every media folder shows its filter field. Fixed in source; not yet seen on a phone.
New, not yet seen in a running build: media folders can be created, renamed, moved and deleted from the Manage dialog, and the server refuses names that leave the media folder.
The paid cloud service is no longer shown anywhere in the interface. The server integration is unchanged.
New, not yet seen: dashboard and automation history have a search field, and Compare uses a searchable version picker. The history and recorded problems pages say "Git remote" in full.

New, not yet seen: the file converter packs and unpacks archives (ZIP, TAR, GZIP), makes PDFs from text, Markdown and pictures, converts Word documents to and from text, makes WAV audio and takes a still picture from a video. Reading PDFs, MP3 output and video-to-video conversion are not offered.
New, not yet seen: a Dashboard tools dialog in edit mode with an outline and bulk actions, find and replace of an entity ID, a check for missing entities, card templates and a preview width.

Fixed: settings saved on the instance now follow the signed-in account, so a second account on the same browser no longer sees or uploads the first one's wording and appearance. Picture layers can only be embedded images or paths on this instance. Error text hides secrets inside values and query strings.

New, not yet seen: update installs show real stages and a recovery card, a Minecraft server page, Ollama unload, model details and a test chat, a support page with a local support bundle, one save bar in the automation, script and scene editors, and a reload button and a framing notice on embedded pages. Eight more blocks have Cantonese.

Seen in a running build (build 96, 390 px wide): the Marketplace list scrolls with its group header pinned, the Personal settings preview scrolls away, and the accessibility panel's rows no longer overlap. Fixed in a later batch, not yet seen: its text size "+" button wrapped onto its own line.
Releases: every release carries the Deploy Assistant installers, and runs replaced by a newer push are cancelled and leave no release.

New, not yet seen in a running build: an authenticator app card on the profile page, an activity tray and a recovery card, time rules and shared defaults for personal settings, information buttons beside settings, panes and a filter pane that can be resized, and starting points for empty editors.
Your appearance choices and personal wording file are now saved on the instance for your account, so another computer picks them up, and they are included in backups.

Fixed: the Minecraft manager no longer reads the SSH config file, bounds what a host sends back, and only touches containers and volumes it created. A missing or truncated automations file can no longer set aside every automation history, and histories set aside can be listed and brought back. An Ollama download that stops early is reported as incomplete. The dashboard import summary shows the real host of an address and lists locks and covers that would be switched.
Fixed: a plain `git clone` of the project now works on Windows, and the local frontend build no longer crashes on a computer with many processors.

Releases: a push that changes only documentation or design files no longer publishes a release, a release with no files is withdrawn, and every release carries the newest Deploy Assistant installers. The 37 releases that had no files were removed.

Minecraft servers can be started on another computer that runs Docker, reached over SSH: add the host with its own key, confirm its fingerprint, then start, stop, read the log and see the address to join. Versions are looked up only when you press Refresh.
Ollama: pull a model with real progress and Cancel, and delete a model.
Help articles: outside links inside articles are plain text, words that had gone missing are back, and every page has a proper title.
A dropped dashboard file can no longer hide a risky button or disguise where a link goes.

Automation history is held to the same rules as dashboard history: a strict address for pushing, a plain warning that anything typed into an automation is kept, and a way to forget an automation's history. History of deleted dashboards can be listed and removed.
The app's name and logo can be applied for everyone. The release notes page replaces the older changes page. School mode can hide the Developer tools entry.
Drawing board: pencil and brush, and very large pictures are refused before they are opened. Converter: YAML merge keys are merged.
Seen in a running build: the Overview header on a phone, and the editable copy opening straight in the editor.
Fixed: on a phone the welcome banner covered the Overview header, so its menu and edit button could not be reached. "Edit cards and layout" now opens the copy in the editor.

A dropped dashboard file shows what it contains before anything is made: outside addresses, custom cards and buttons that would call a service. Imports start hidden from the rail and visible to administrators only.
Dashboard history: set an address and push a dashboard with all its tabs, forget a dashboard's history, and a deleted dashboard's history is set aside, not reused.
Help: every remaining help link opens inside the interface, including on the sign-in page. All 1,392 integration pages and their pictures are included. Community links are removed.
Passkeys: a flood of empty attempts can no longer stop passkey sign-in, and removing a passkey needs a recent password sign-in.
New tools: a file converter and a drawing board. New pages: Ollama servers and models, renaming the app and its logo, and release notes.
Personal settings: language cards, playfulness sliders that change real messages, a switch for emojis in dialogs, one thing at a time, and School mode.
Fixed: a section could stay stuck half open, first-run setup could leave both buttons off, and a list's header checkbox could leave hidden rows selected.
Builds: a documentation push on top of code no longer leaves that code unbuilt.
Dashboards: built-in pages such as Overview have "Edit cards and layout", which makes an editable copy and opens it in the editor. On a phone the edit button sits beside the menu.
Dashboards can be exported and imported, and a dashboard file dropped anywhere on the window is imported at once as a new dashboard, with Undo.
Every dashboard has its own history, and so has every tab: see what changed, compare two versions and go back. The dashboard's repository carries its tabs with it.
Help links open a copy of the article inside the interface. Nothing opens a new tab or another browser for help. The first 44 articles are included, with their source and licence.
Passkeys: sign in with a fingerprint, face or security key on a secure address, beside the password, which stays. Add and remove passkeys on the profile page.
The automation editor moves: cards open and close smoothly, new steps slide in, results fade in. All of it respects the reduce-motion setting.
A page for Minecraft servers under Settings: define servers with a guided form. Starting them comes next.
First-run setup no longer offers a cloud restore or links to outside sites, and nothing contacts an outside map service until you press a button that says so.
Backups: a storage location that needs encryption is off while encryption is off, and a stored key is never replaced or removed without asking.
The selection bar is on the Automations and Scripts lists and no longer covers the last rows. Unknown pages under Settings show a not-found screen.
Fixed: a debug log could have contained the key file used by Google setup. Secrets are masked more widely in the setup wizards.
The launch screen no longer says the project is from the Open Home Foundation.

Google setup: a wizard under Settings sets Google up once for every Google integration. A service account key file can switch on the needed services (used once, never stored), the page shows the return address to copy, and the client file is read by dropping it.
Read aloud only ever uses a voice that runs on the device, like the narrator.
First-run setup shows password strength and a preview of dates and units, and asks you to review before saving. The lock wizard can try the new lock before it is saved.
Run now, for automations and scripts, says that the saved version runs, asks first, and reports the result. It is off while there are unsaved changes.
The entity dialog no longer repeats the lock and appearance tools, and an unavailable date no longer leaves it empty. Maintenance counts one row per device.
Fixed: a crafted link name could leave the link page blank.
A link that opens a page of this interface from outside now asks first, shows where it goes and what it passes on, and does nothing until you choose.
Date, time and calendar dialogs follow the time zone chosen in the profile. The time dialog has real spin controls and the date grid can be walked with the arrow keys.

The colour picker applies a typed colour when you finish typing, not at every letter, and stores a drag a few times instead of at every move. Fonts and accessibility: fixes for narrow screens, focus, and a font that is not on the device.

The selection bar sits at the bottom, counts only the rows shown, and says when ticked rows are hidden by the filter. Exports keep duplicate column names apart and say when rows were cut. Outside links in notifications show their host.
Group dialogs ask before switching covers, locks or valves. The image dialog no longer has a share button, because the shared address carried an access code.
Tabs and the search of everything follow the language mode, with Cantonese written. Open a tab lists the tools. Starting, connection lost and no-access screens are redrawn.
Fixed: builds 64 and 65 were published without images, because a push that changed many files was mistaken for a documentation-only push. Build 66 is the first with images again.
The narrator only ever uses a voice that runs on the device. If there is none it stays silent, so spoken text is never sent anywhere.

Choose step: a disabled condition is left out of a test, old results are cleared when the step is edited, an option that can never run is marked, and Run asks first. The automation editor has an on and off switch, a Check button, and a strip that shows its history.
The entity dialog has a tab row and a tools block (lock, appearance, read aloud, export), and no longer shows the state twice.
The script editor is redrawn with a mode selector, Run now and See past runs. Maintenance opens with what needs you. The error and loading screens are redrawn.
Tabs: fixes for screen readers and the keyboard, and the search shrinks to a button on a narrow screen. The search of everything works for people who are not administrators.
Text that carries links keeps the personal wording on its plain parts.
Fixed: with a wording file loaded, the tip under Settings showed an error instead of its text. Text that carries links is now left as it is.
The choose step in the automation editor can test and run one option, the default actions, or the whole step. Automations link to their history.
The phone bar, the locks and the wording card follow the language mode. The phone sheet keeps the tab order and pins. Tab order and pins are kept in the page history.

Notifications no longer guess a severity from their words. A failed dismissal is reported and not hidden. Exported cells that start a formula are made safe without turning numbers into text. Labels use the selection bar for deleting.

Entity dialogs for date, time, date and time, sun, image, calendar, setup step, siren, lawn mower, remote, group, automation, script and conversation are redrawn, and the shared controls for alarm, climate, lock, fan, vacuum and water heater follow the boards.
Accessibility has line spacing and letter spacing. A fonts dialog lists only typefaces that ship with the app or are on the device. The appearance editor has its own colour picker.
The person dialog no longer links to an outside map service. About names the install type through the wording file.
Language mode changes real text: Personal settings can be read in English, Cantonese or both. The phone bar, the locks and the wording card have their Cantonese written and will follow next.
A spoken narrator, off by default, reads the name of the control in focus with the browser's own voice. Two attention modes are added: a small clock, and an offer to go back to the page you were on.
Tabs can be dragged into a new order and pinned. The search of everything lists settings and entities with a live switch in the result.

Dismissed notifications are kept for thirty days and every dismissal can be undone. The page export has a tab-separated format and can take only the ticked rows. A selection bar shows what will change before it changes anything.

Entity dialogs for climate, cover, counter, lock, alarm, camera, media player, vacuum, fan, light, weather, sensor, update, person, timer, humidifier, water heater and valve are started on their boards.
The automation editor shows triggers, conditions and actions as three named cards.
Thirteen more defects found by review are fixed, in backups, voice assistants, energy setup, apps, automations, their history and past runs.
Devices and Entities have their filters as chips beside the search, a tick box on every row and a line under the list; Labels has its Create button beside the title.

Started on their boards: Backups and backup settings, voice assistants and one assistant's page, what is exposed to assistants, the cloud account, energy setup, apps and the app store, the list of automations, their history and repositories, past runs, MQTT, Thread and Bluetooth.

Six more defects found by review are fixed: Profile tabs no longer reload the page, the people on the sign-in page are real buttons, the Zigbee list has its way to the map, a device list is no longer cut between a device and its children, the Logs filters come back on, and Statistics sorts and groups by area again.
Statistics and Scenes can be sorted and grouped again, and Statistics keeps its search, sorting and grouping in the page address.
Sign-in, first-run setup, About, Profile, Helpers, the settings of one entity, and the Zigbee, Z-Wave and Matter pages are started on their boards.
Nine defects found by review are fixed: People, Zones, Blueprints, Repairs, Logs, Updates and the scene editor.

More pages on their boards: Integrations (status on each card, filter chips), an integration's own page, Devices (what needs attention, offline and low battery marked), one device, Entities (a live state column), Areas and one area, Labels, Scenes as cards and the scene editor, Scripts with Run and Stop, Zones, Blueprints, Dashboards, People, Users, Tags, Updates, Repairs and Logs.

Developer tools: Events shows a live feed, YAML shows whether the configuration is valid and reloads each kind, Statistics lists problems first, Assist shows what a sentence was understood as. Labs is a grid of switches, and Restart is one list of choices with one button.
The form that runs an action draws each field as a row with its own switch.
An installation set up by an earlier build no longer logs an error about analytics at start.

Nothing is sent out any more. The analytics integration, its page and its first-run step are gone, the supervisor's crash reports and diagnostics are off, and the buttons that reported an issue or gave feedback are removed.

Problems are kept on this system instead. Settings, System, Problem log lists every warning and error, one entry per problem with a count and when it was first and last seen. They are files in a Git repository in the configuration folder, with passwords, tokens, addresses and other private values removed. Nothing leaves the system unless you add a remote yourself.
A wording file that loads gets a short celebration over the whole window and a sound; one that is refused gets a different sound and a clear message.
Storage, General, Hardware and Network are drawn to their boards, and so are the States, Actions and Template pages of the developer tools. General has one Save and one Discard.

Everyday pages start on their boards: Lights opens with how many are on and a card for each room; Security shows each alarm with arm and disarm; Climate draws the first thermostat large; the Map lists where everyone is; Activity, History, To-do, Calendar and Energy gain a large title and a line of facts; Home shows power use when energy is set up.
The Network page lays its cards out in two columns on a wide screen.

On a phone there is a bar at the bottom: Home, Search, Pages, Access and Menu. Pages opens a sheet of the open pages with a search, New tab, and closing by button or swipe, with Undo. A slim bar at the top switches between open pages.
The pattern workbench on a phone has three tabs and More, one chip for the flags, and a footer that gets out of the way of the keyboard. On a wide screen the flags are named chips and the tabs wrap.
Holding an element shows a ring and opens a sheet on a phone; on a wide screen the menu sits beside the element and each tool has a one-letter shortcut.
The lock wizard has six steps with a progress line and a QR code for the one-time code. The unlock prompt counts down a wait, and the list of locks filters, selects several and shows the time left.

Personal settings are grouped, show what each control reaches, and gain quiet hours for sounds. Guided setup lists what is set up first, and its last step offers one action: reload or restart. The guidance note in setup dialogs opens as a sheet.

Fifteen of the browser's own blocking boxes are replaced by messages and dialogs of the interface. Deleting an energy source, removing a Matter fabric, resetting a Thread border router and turning off a second sign-in step ask twice.
Turning on a preview feature with its backup switch on no longer fails when automatic backups are not set up. The backup is kept on this system.

Guided setup draws real fields for 223 of the 240 integrations it lists, up from 10: text, numbers, switches, choices, templates, durations and entity pickers, and a first step that asks which kind of item to add where an integration has several.

Guided setup: integrations that had to be written by hand in YAML can be created from Settings, Guided setup, or from Add integration. Each one gets a step-by-step form, a review of what will be written, and a note on whether a reload or a restart follows. Most still show one YAML box that is checked before saving, not drawn fields. The setup dialogs of other integrations gain a short guidance note with a link to the documentation.

Locks on single elements choose their own way in: a PIN, a password, a one-time code, or a mix of them, each lock with its own. A wizard opens beside the element, a keypad or the keyboard enters the PIN, and the Lock tool lists every lock. A lock is a speed bump for fun, not security; clearing this site's storage removes them all.

Personal settings: a page under Settings for sounds, low stimulation, the focus spotlight and reduced motion, with a search. Language mode and the two playfulness levels are saved and shown in a preview; the rest of the interface does not follow them yet.
On a phone, the menu of an element scrolls inside the screen, the New tab list stays on the screen, every tab shows its close button, and side panels stop at the visible height.
The event filter in Developer tools has the pattern workbench.
Developer tools are back on the navigation rail, just above Settings, for administrators.
The pattern workbench fits a phone: it takes the visible screen instead of the space under the field, follows the keyboard, and its switches start at the left.
On a phone, resting a finger on an element opens its menu, where a right-click does on a computer. Text fields keep the phone's own menu, and cards that act on a hold keep theirs.
The search of a media library has the pattern workbench. A pattern is tested against the titles in the open folder; plain text still goes to the media source.
`host.bat` waits properly when it is started from a Git shell. It used to give up at once and report a failure although the container had started. `compose.yaml` runs build 46.
The operating system image started on VMware Workstation; the README says how, and how to clone this repository on Windows.

Locks on single elements: right-click anything and choose Lock this element. It stops taking clicks and keys and gets a dashed outline. The Lock tool lists the locked elements of the page and unlocks each one by a hold, or all of them with the PIN.
The README shows captures from a running instance.
Tools: a Colour tab that reads one colour in every notation, names the nearest named colour and says how well text reads on it.
Notifications as a page, with a search and dismissing one, the selected ones or all. The notification drawer links to it.
The rail has an Assist button at its top.
Lists: the icon of each row sits on a small tile, and a device row names its maker and model under the device.
What changed: this list inside the interface, under Settings, About, with a search, a range of days and the commit behind each entry. It ships with the build and opens without a connection.

About: the version and build time of this project, where its updates come from, that it is free, and that it is independent of the Open Home Foundation. The links to merchandise and to the upstream issue tracker are gone; Report a problem opens this project's issues.
Tabs: close the tabs that match a search, or the ones that do not, with counts and Undo.
Automations: a visible test button on every condition and on every Choose option.
The search at the top is a real search field with the pattern workbench; what is typed or built there opens the search of everything with that text.

Interface: page tools in the header of every settings page. Search this page (with the pattern workbench), edit appearance, read aloud, history, export, lock and help; one button on a narrow screen. Section tabs moved to a row under the header, and wide screens have a footer line.
Tools: a Base64 toolkit for text and files, with strict and lenient decoding and data URLs.
Home: large cards for a room's lights, the thermostat, the locks and what is playing.
Anything that destroys data is confirmed with two keys and a slide, not one button.
System: a card about the running system and its sections as a grid. Pages reached from Settings show where they sit above their title.
Dialogs: a row at the foot of every dialog with Search this dialog, Edit appearance and Lock.
Fixed: read aloud, copy the text and export left out text that a component shows through a slot, which was most of a page.
Home opens with a greeting for the time of day, a sentence about the home made from its real state, and buttons for the scenes used most.
The page tools, the footer and the lock are on history, activity, media, to-do lists, calendar and the developer tools. Dashboards have the footer and the lock.
Settings home: a large title, a search of the sections, banners for updates and repairs, and the sections as a grid of cards that say what each holds now.
The rail is compact by default. The top bar has a language button and the user's picture.
List pages under Settings: where the page sits and its title in the header, a large title with a summary line, rows as rounded cards, and an export button beside the table settings.
The menu on any element has Export this page, History of changes and Lock this page.
Export a page as CSV, JSON, Markdown, plain text or HTML, or print it.
Lock a page with the lock button or Ctrl+Shift+L; unlock with a hold or a PIN.
History of local changes to appearance, accessibility and open tabs, with undo.
Help articles that ship with the interface.
Automations: a History tab with every version of every automation; test one or many, run one or many, compare, make live, export, and commit everything to the master repository.
Automations: a Git repository for each automation and a master repository (new integration `automation_repos`). Every save is a commit.
Fixed: the test button on a Choose option failed when the option had conditions, because the server tests one condition at a time.
Appearance editor for any element: right-click, Ctrl+Shift+E or the paint button, then change fill layers, text, shape, accent and size for that element or every one of its kind.
A menu on every element, with a filter and working shortcuts.
Private vocabulary: load your own JSON wording file from Profile, Localization, or drop it anywhere in the window. Checked in full, kept in the browser only, replace and clear.
Hosting: `compose.yaml`, `host.sh` and `host.bat` start the published image in one step.
The published image (build 26) was run from the registry and driven through first-run setup.
Fixed: the production build failed on the pattern workbench (builds 23 to 25 have no images).
Root README, licence, notice, contributing, security and conduct files.
Feature status page and roadmap.
Interface: Material Design 3 colour scales and surfaces, Google Sans Flex, the navigation rail, the floating pane, borderless cards and pill tabs.
Interface: version and build time at the foot of the rail.
Interface: the bar of open pages. Every page starts open, a closed tab stays closed, and the New tab catalog lists every page, searches them and can reopen them all.
The command search opens with Ctrl+Shift+F and from a Search button in the top bar.

Interface: accessibility tools on a top bar button and Alt+A. Text size, contrast, reduced motion, a focus ring that follows the focused control, larger targets, reading the page aloud and keyboard help.
Fixed: vendored font files were altered by line-ending conversion on commit.

Interface: every search field has a pattern workbench button, and every list accepts a regular expression written as `/pattern/flags`. Plain text stays the default. The workbench shows which items of the list a pattern matches. Seen working on the New tab catalog in the demo build.

Design: every page of the product is drawn. 153 boards on 11 canvases of at most 15 boards, including a Git repository per automation, a master repository, an automation history manager and test buttons on Choose options and conditions.
Builds in progress are no longer cancelled by a newer push.
The repository: upstream frontend, core, supervisor, operating system (with Buildroot), landing page and version feed, each vendored in its own folder at a pinned release.

A release workflow that publishes one tagged release per push to `main` and builds the frontend wheel, core, machine, landing page and supervisor images, a multi-architecture container image, the update feed, and operating system images for Raspberry Pi 3, 4 and 5 and virtual machines.
An update feed on the `channel` branch. The supervisor and the operating system read it instead of the upstream feed.
`build.bat`, `build-installer.bat`, `build.sh` and dependency installers.
The design canvas: 48 boards covering the everyday screens and every required feature.
Build 1: frontend wheel, both supervisor images, both core images, all machine images and the multi-architecture container image built and are publicly pullable. The update feed is live.
Not verified: operating system images (still building when this was written), a real boot on a Raspberry Pi or in VirtualBox, an update from one build to the next, the Windows scripts.
